note.headline: Tech keeps sliding; trend, fear and thin breadth still say stand aside

summary.thesis: Both SPY and QQQ are in downtrends, below their 50- and 200-day averages. Fear is 'elevated' as of Nov 24, and breadth is 8%. Trend, fear and breadth all point the same way.
summary.decision: Stand aside for new buying, both long-term and swing.
summary.act_at: A QQQ close above 682.54, its 200-day average and the market gate, ends the tech downtrend. A QQQ close below 608.45 or an SPY close below 689.81 would set a new 1-month low, meaning the decline would be continuing.

note.happening: SPY closed at 716.7, down 0.29% from 718.78. It is down 1.85% over 5 days and 7.2% over 20 days. QQQ closed at 633.93, down 0.65% from 638.1. It is down 3.88% over 5 days and 12.63% over 20 days. Both peaked for the month on Oct 28, at 772.31 for SPY and 725.61 for QQQ. Both hit their 1-month lows on Nov 20, at 689.81 and 608.45. The past year's highest closes were on Oct 6: 779.09 for SPY and 759.66 for QQQ. Q3 GDP (second estimate) with corporate profits, and October Personal Income and Outlays (including PCE inflation), were scheduled for today at 08:30. Their results are not in DATA, and no news was recorded since the last note.
note.business: Trend: both indexes sit below their 50-day averages (SPY 757.85, QQQ 707.02) and their 200-day averages (SPY 730.77, QQQ 682.54), so the trend is down. Tech is weaker than the broad market. QQQ is 7.7% below its 200-day average, while SPY is 2.0% below its own. Fear: the VIX reading is in the 'elevated' band (20–30) and sits at the 95 percentile of its 252-day range. That reading is from Nov 24, because the Nov 25 value isn't stored yet. (General knowledge: the VIX reflects the market swings options traders expect over the next month.) Breadth: only 8% of stocks are above their 50-day averages, so the selling is broad, not limited to a few big names. Taken together, the market is falling, falling widely, and nervous. None of the three readings supports new buying yet. Both indexes are still above their Nov 20 lows: QQQ is 4.0% above and SPY is 3.8% above, so that floor is holding for now.

worth.text: This is a market note. No valuation is implied, and the levels below are price-trend markers only.
worth.key_assumption: No valuation is implied. The levels are price-trend markers only.

bull: Both indexes are still above their Nov 20 1-month lows (QQQ 608.45, SPY 689.81), so the recent low is holding.
SPY is only 2.0% below its 200-day average of 730.77, much closer to its long-term trend line than QQQ is to its own.

Breadth at 8% and a VIX reading at the 95 percentile mean the readings are stretched. (General knowledge: readings this stretched have sometimes come near short-term turning points, but they do not mark one by themselves.)
bear: QQQ is 7.7% below its 200-day average and 11.5% below its 50-day average, so tech is in a downtrend on both time frames.
Breadth fell from 10% in the last note to 8%, so fewer stocks are holding up.
Fear is still 'elevated' and up 0.9 over 5 days as of Nov 24. Both indexes fell again today, and QQQ is down 12.63% over 20 days.

QQQ 1-month low (Nov 20). A close below it would set a new 1-month low, meaning the decline would be continuing.
QQQ 50-day average. A close above it would put tech's short-term trend back up and pass the pipeline's 'QQQ above its 50-day average' check.
QQQ 1-month high (Oct 28). A close above it would mean the tech pullback is fully recovered.
SPY 1-month low (Nov 20). A close below it would set a new 1-month low, meaning the decline would be continuing.
SPY 200-day average. A close above it would put the broad market's long-term trend back up.

note.headline: Tesla slips 1.18% to 380.14, stuck under resistance; still avoid

summary.thesis: Tesla's sales have stalled, and its margins and cash flow are shrinking, yet the stock trades near the top of its own valuation history at 418.3 times earnings.
summary.decision: Long-term: avoid. Swing: wait, because the price sits just under a resistance zone that has turned it back 9 times and there is no trend.
summary.act_at: Re-examine near 293.94 only if margin recovers; no swing trade until a close above 404.4

note.happening: Tesla closed at 380.14, down 1.18% on the day. That is just below a resistance zone at 380.15–389.95, a price band where rallies have stalled 9 times. The 20-, 50- and 200-day averages (382.15, 377.17, 381.15) are all flat, and the trend is marked as a range. There is no new news since yesterday's note, which covered a reported SpaceX merger. The next earnings report is due 2027-01-27.
note.business: The latest filing (2026-10-22) points to a business that has slowed. Revenue in the latest quarter was -0.17% versus a year earlier, down from 15.78% growth two quarters ago. Operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) fell to 3.35% from 4.74%. Trailing free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) halved, from 6.8B to 3.3B. Inventory is up 15% while quarterly sales are up 0%. Unsold cars can force price cuts that squeeze margins further. Returns on new investment have dropped to 5¢ per dollar a year from 33¢ three years ago, so heavy spending is not paying back yet. What is not at risk is the balance sheet: net cash is 37.5B and total liquidity is 45.4B, against 8.0B of debt. Share dilution is small at 0.43%. The reported SpaceX merger changes governance and sentiment, not demand or margins, unless terms are filed.

worth.text: At 380.14, Tesla is valued at about 1503.0B. That is 14.5 times sales and 418.3 times trailing earnings per share of 0.91. A cash-flow model (DCF: today's value of future cash) built on trailing free cash flow of 3.3B and a 9.9% discount rate gives 20.17 / 24.93 / 45.0 per share for bear / base / bull. Even assuming 30% starting growth, it reaches only 45.31. The filings risk note says the price needs about 51% a year growth, while the company has delivered 3% a year over 3 years. Against its own history, the price-to-sales ratio is at the 75th percentile of the past 5 years. That method maps to 203.8 / 293.94 / 399.81, so the stock sits close to the top of that range. The gap between the two methods comes down to one thing. The DCF prices today's small cash flow, while the history method assumes the market keeps paying the rich sales multiples it has paid before. With sales flat and margins falling, a fair range is the low-to-middle part of Tesla's own history.
worth.key_assumption: With flat quarterly sales and operating margin down to 3.35%, the market values Tesla in the low-to-middle part of its 5-year price-to-sales range rather than near the 399.81 top.

bull: Net cash of 37.5B and liquidity of 45.4B give Tesla room to keep investing through a slow patch.
Revenue over the last 12 months still grew 8.3%, to 103.6B from 95.6B.
Analysts' next-year EPS growth assumption is 25%; if delivered, the DCF value rises toward the 34.01–45.31 range shown for 20–30% starting growth.
bear: The price needs about 51% a year growth, versus 3% a year delivered over 3 years.
Trailing free cash flow fell to 3.3B from 6.8B, and operating margin fell to 3.35% from 4.74%.
Inventory is up 15% while quarterly sales are up 0%, which can force price cuts that hurt margins further.

levels.what: Today's close. It sits near the own-history top of 399.81 and far above the DCF base of 24.93, so value gives the price no support here.
Bottom of the nearest support zone (363.86–368.76), where buyers have stepped in 4 times. A close below it points to the next zone at 349.24–354.14.
Middle of the own-history price-to-sales range. Re-examine here only if the 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin back above 4.74%.

longterm.why: Sales growth, margins, cash flow and returns on investment are all weakening, while the price sits near the top of its own valuation history. The internal committee call is Reduce, and the business grade is D.

swing.why: The price sits just under resistance at 380.15–389.95 (9 touches), the averages are flat and the trend is a range, so there is no clean setup. No trade until a close above 404.4, or until a pullback holds at 363.86–368.76.

decision.timing: No new long-term position before the 2027-01-27 report. Options price an 11.2% move by 2026-12-18 and a 19.6% move by 2027-02-19, which covers the report. Recent actual swings (72.9) have been bigger than what options imply (53.6), and any filed merger terms could move the price before earnings.

change_mind: The 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin back above 4.74% and quarterly revenue growth back above 0% versus a year earlier.
Trailing free cash flow climbs back toward 6.8B while inventory growth falls back to the pace of sales growth.
The price falls toward the 293.94 own-history midpoint with margins stable, which would make a long-term look worthwhile; a close below 363.86 would instead strengthen the avoid.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still avoid; the 1.18% drop to 380.14 left the price below the 380.15–389.95 resistance zone and still near the top of its own valuation range, while the trend label moved from down to range.
note.label: Research, not advice.

note.headline: NVIDIA falls 3.91% to 149.30 as comeback rally fizzles; still hold above 147.13

summary.thesis: The business is still growing fast and making a lot of cash. The share price already assumes cash flow growth of about 18.9% a year. What could go wrong is margins falling from their peak and customers paying their bills later.
summary.decision: Hold for the long term and stay out of a swing trade while the price sits on its only nearby support zone in a downtrend.
summary.act_at: Wait on a close below 147.13; buy at 116.97; trim near 226.93

note.happening: NVDA fell 3.91% to 149.30. It now sits inside the 147.13–150.47 zone, below a falling 20-day average of 172.48. Headlines reported that the rally on Jensen Huang's return 'fizzled' and that worries about AI spending came back. They also reported that Trump called a pardon for Huang 'an option'. Our data has no earnings date, so there is no fixed event ahead.
note.business: Most of today's news is about governance and mood, not about the business. Huang's return, the reported pardon talk, the Megaspeed questions and the succession debate are all in that group. None of these headlines reports lower orders or a lost customer. The business numbers in the last filing (2026-08-26) are strong. Sales over the last twelve months were 303.0B, up from 165.2B. Latest-quarter sales grew 105.85% from a year earlier. Operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) rose to 65.21% from 58.09%. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) rose to 127.0B from 72.0B. Cash exceeds debt by 23.2B. Analysts keep raising forecasts: next-year earnings per share is 16.61, up 4.3% in 30 days. Two things are genuinely at risk. First, the margin sits at the top of its 5-year range of 16–65%. Second, unpaid customer bills grew 127% while sales grew 106%. That can mean sales were pulled forward or customers are under strain. One reported headline, which our data marks as speculative, says Big Tech faces a 'spending squeeze'. That would matter for demand if it were confirmed. Insiders sold $946.6M of shares outside pre-set plans. This affects confidence, not the business.

worth.text: Using a cash flow model (it values the company on the cash it is expected to generate in future years), the price of 149.30 implies free cash flow growth of about 18.9% a year at the start. If that starting growth is 20%, the model gives 155.64. At 30% it gives 226.93, which is the base case. The gap between methods comes down almost entirely to that starting growth figure and to whether the 65% margin holds. If the operating margin falls to 48%, the value drops to 116.97. At 32% it is 78.3. Earnings multiples (price divided by profit per share) look low: 18.8 times trailing earnings and 9.0 times next year's forecast. Price-to-sales is 11.9, against a peer median of 13.6, and sits at the 4.0th percentile of its own 5-year history. The history-based price-to-sales method puts value at 217.35–411.04. The cheap multiples rest on peak margins and forecasts that rose quickly, with next-year earnings estimates up 27.7% in 90 days. So the range starts at the margin-fade value.
worth.key_assumption: Operating margin stays near 65.21% rather than fading toward 48%, while free cash flow grows from 127.0B at a starting rate above the 18.9% the price implies.

bull: The price is only 9.0 times next year's forecast earnings of 16.61, and that forecast is up 27.7% in 90 days.
Free cash flow rose to 127.0B from 72.0B, and cash exceeds debt by 23.2B.
Price-to-sales of 11.9 sits at the 4.0th percentile of its own 5-year range and below the peer median of 13.6.
bear: Unpaid customer bills grew 127% against sales growth of 106%. That points to sales pulled forward or customers under strain.
Operating margin of 65.21% is at the top of its 16–65% five-year range. A fall to 48% gives a model value of 116.97, below today's price.
The trend is down: the price is below the 50-day average of 203.65, and insiders sold $946.6M outside pre-set plans.

levels.what: Bottom of the support zone the price is sitting in (147.13–150.47). A close below it moves the call to wait, with the next support at 122.83–126.17.
Model value if the operating margin falls to 48%. Buy at 116.97, because that price already allows for a large margin fade.
Base-case cash flow value. Trim near it, because at that price the market would be paying for 30% starting growth and the full current margin.

longterm.why: The automated rule says 'Buy now' and the committee says 'Hold'. The price already assumes about 18.9% growth on a peak margin, and the slow-payment risk is unresolved. So the call is hold, not add.

swing.why: The trend is down, with lower highs and lower lows, and the 20-day average of 172.48 is falling. A typical day's range is 13.38, which would break through any tight stop placed below 147.13. No trade until the price closes above 171.33, the top of the resistance zone with 4 touches.

decision.timing: Our data has no earnings date. The options data is from 2026-11-24 and priced off 155.38, so its expected moves are out of date after today's drop. Until the next quarterly filing shows whether the 65.21% margin and customer payments hold up, the levels above set the timing, not a calendar date.

change_mind: A close below 147.13 moves the long-term call from hold to wait, with buying considered only toward 122.83–126.17 or 116.97.
If the next filing shows operating margin below the prior 58.09%, or customer bills again growing faster than sales, the call moves toward trim. If both look healthy, the call moves to add.
If the next-year EPS consensus falls back below 15.91 (its level 30 days ago), the cheap 9.0 forward multiple can no longer be trusted, and the call moves from hold to wait.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still hold, because the close of 149.30 stayed above the 147.13 bottom of the support zone despite today's 3.91% drop.
note.label: Research, not advice.

note.headline: AMD slips 1.75% to 406.03, sitting on support, still above fair value

summary.thesis: AMD is growing faster and earning more, but at 406.03 the price assumes 51.8% yearly cash-flow growth, well above every fair-value estimate in our data.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for 333.38 or lower. Swing: no trade while the downtrend holds.
summary.act_at: Long-term buy case starts at 333.38; swing only after a close above 451.0

note.happening: AMD fell 1.75% to 406.03. That puts it just above the 391.92–403.54 support zone and below its 20-day (489.22), 50-day (548.35) and 200-day (432.96) averages, so the trend is down. There is no news since the last note, and the next earnings report is on 2027-02-02.
note.business: The business itself is getting stronger. Sales grew 44.68% from a year earlier in the latest quarter, up from 37.85% two quarters ago. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, rose to 17.72% from 8.78%. Free cash flow, the cash left after investment, reached 7.1B over the last twelve months, up from 5.4B. The company holds 8.7B more cash than debt, so its finances are not at risk. Analysts raised next-year earnings estimates by 11.3% in 30 days. Two things are at risk. First, inventory rose 57% while quarterly sales rose 45% (both against a year earlier). Unsold chips can force price cuts, and that would hit margins. Second, the 18% operating margin is at the top of its 5-year range of -2% to 22%, and margins this high often come back down. The recent price drop looks like a change in mood, not in the business: the tech market is in a downtrend, and put open interest is 2.41 times call interest. Nothing in the latest filing shows demand weakening.

worth.text: At 406.03, AMD trades at 88.5 times last year's earnings, 23.0 times next year's expected earnings, and 14.7 times sales. The peer median is 12.3 times sales, and AMD's own price-to-sales ratio is in the 88th percentile of its last five years. A cash-flow model (DCF), which values today's free cash flow of 7.1B grown over time, gives 147.69 to 225.08, with 189.77 in the middle. AMD's own price-to-sales history gives 179.24 to 333.38. To justify today's price, cash flow would need to start growing at 51.8% a year. The model caps starting growth at 30%, and even at that cap the value is only 189.77. The gap between the two views comes down to one question: does analysts' 118% next-year EPS growth last, or fade like normal growth? Margins matter too. If operating margin fell back to 13%, the model value drops to 100.01.
worth.key_assumption: Starting cash-flow growth: the price implies 51.8% a year while the model caps it at 30%, so the price only makes sense if the 118% jump in next-year EPS growth keeps going.

bull: Growth is speeding up: quarterly sales grew 44.68% from a year earlier, up from 37.85% two quarters ago.
Profitability nearly doubled: operating margin rose to 17.72% from 8.78%, and free cash flow climbed to 7.1B from 5.4B.
Estimates are rising fast: next-year EPS of 17.64 was raised 11.3% in 30 days, which puts the stock at 23.0 times next year's earnings.
bear: The price needs 51.8% starting cash-flow growth. Even at the model's 30% cap, the value is 189.77, far below 406.03.
Inventory rose 57% against 45% sales growth. If that leads to price cuts and operating margin falls to 13%, the model value drops to 100.01.
The stock costs 14.7 times sales, above the peer median of 12.3 and in the 88th percentile of its own 5-year range.

levels.what: Today's close. It is above every valuation method, so it is not a buy price.
Bottom of the 391.92–403.54 support zone. A close below it would point to the next zone at 347.18–358.8, and the price would still be above fair value.
Top of the fair-value range, based on AMD's own price-to-sales history. The value case for buying starts here.

longterm.why: The business is strong and improving, but the price assumes far more growth than any method supports. Wait for 333.38 or lower, or for results that support much faster lasting growth.

swing.why: The trend is down: lower highs and lower lows, and the price is below all three averages. The average daily range (ATR) of 46.51 is wider than the whole 391.92–403.54 support zone, so a stop there would sit inside normal daily swings. No trade until a close above 451.0, the top of the 424.03–451.0 resistance zone.

decision.timing: The 2027-02-02 report is more than two months away. Options price an 18.6% move by 2026-12-18, and the most put open interest sits at the 400 strike, so mood alone could push the price below the support zone before the report.

change_mind: A price at or below 333.38 would bring AMD into its fair-value range and would turn the long-term action toward buy.
In the 2027-02-02 report, a beat of the 3.3 next-quarter EPS estimate together with inventory growth falling back below sales growth (now 57% vs 45%) would ease the margin risk.
A close above 451.0 would break the 424.03–451.0 resistance and end the swing no-trade stance. A close below 391.92 would confirm the selloff toward 347.18–358.8.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait and no trade, because the price fell 1.75% to 406.03 and remains above the 333.38 top of the fair-value range.
note.label: Research, not advice.

note.headline: Amazon drops 3.12% to 244.43, below its 200-day average; still waiting for 238.65

summary.thesis: Amazon is growing and its profit margin is widening, but it is burning cash and growth is slowing, so the stock is not cheap enough yet against its own history.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait, and buy only near 238.65. Swing: no trade while the downtrend holds.

note.happening: Amazon fell 3.12% to 244.43. That puts it just below its 200-day average of 245.78 and keeps it in a downtrend. The only news was a speculative TechCrunch report that Amazon and Meta are in talks over the AI agent Muse. The next earnings report is due 2027-02-04.
note.business: Today's drop changes sentiment, not the business. Nothing new has been filed since 2026-10-30, and the Muse talks are only reported, with no numbers attached. The latest figures are mixed. Profitability improved: operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, rose to 13.09% from 11.02%. But growth is slowing. Sales grew 12.09% in the latest quarter, down from 16.61% two quarters earlier, and only 0.67% over the prior quarter. Cash is the bigger worry. Free cash flow, the cash left after spending on the business, swung to -46.9B from 10.6B a year earlier. Debt now exceeds cash by 66.7B. There is no immediate funding risk, because liquidity (cash plus credit it can draw) stands at 114.2B. One more warning from the filings: unpaid customer bills rose 61% while sales rose 12%, which may mean sales were pulled forward. The 13% margin is also at the top of its 5-year range. Revenue scale is not at risk. What is at risk is margins and cash generation.

worth.text: There is no discounted-cash-flow value because free cash flow is negative. That leaves one method: what investors have paid for Amazon's sales over the past 5 years. That range runs from 187.93 to 265.96, with a middle of 238.65. At 244.43, the price is slightly above the middle. The stock trades at 19.8 times past earnings. On next year's estimates it trades at 22.9 times, a higher figure because analysts expect earnings per share of 10.67 next year against 12.8 this year. Price to sales is 3.3, against a peer median of 6.3, so Amazon looks cheap next to GOOGL, META and MSFT. It is not cheap against its own past: it sits at the 65th percentile of its own 5-year range. The filings also note that the price needs about 33% yearly growth, compared with 13% delivered over 3 years. Which yardstick applies drives the whole gap: Amazon's own history or its peers' multiples.
worth.key_assumption: Amazon's price-to-sales stays within its own 5-year range instead of moving toward the peer median of 6.3.

bull: Operating margin rose to 13.09% from 11.02%, so more of each sales dollar is turning into profit.
Price to sales of 3.3 is well below the peer median of 6.3, and growth-adjusted it scores 0.62 against peers.
Analysts raised next-year earnings estimates by 1.4% over 30 days, and liquidity of 114.2B covers the cash burn for now.
bear: Free cash flow fell to -46.9B from 10.6B a year earlier, and debt exceeds cash by 66.7B.
Quarterly sales growth slowed to 12.09% from 16.61% two quarters ago, while unpaid customer bills rose 61%.
Next-quarter earnings estimates were cut 2.6% in 30 days, and the price closed below its 200-day average of 245.78 in a downtrend.

levels.what: The middle of the own-history value range, inside the 233.59–238.97 support zone, a price area where buyers stepped in 3 times before. This is the main buy level.
The bottom of the deeper 226.88–232.99 support zone (4 touches). This is a level to add if the first buy is filled and the zone holds.
The top of the own-history value range. No buying above it.

longterm.why: At 244.43 the price is still above the 238.65 middle of its value range, and the cash burn and slowing growth are unresolved. The business grade is D and the committee call is 'Reduce'.

swing.why: The stock is in a downtrend, below its 20-day (257.19), 50-day (255.12) and 200-day (245.78) averages. Its typical daily move, the average true range, is 10.45, so the nearest support at 233.59–238.97 sits about one normal day away. No trade unless the price holds 233.59–238.97, or closes above 258.08, the top of the resistance zone that has turned the price back 7 times.

decision.timing: The 2027-02-04 report is the next real test. Options expiring 2027-02-19, after that report, price in a move of about 15.8%, against 8.3% for 2026-12-18, so any buy before the report starts at 238.65 and not higher.

change_mind: A filing showing free cash flow better than -46.9B, with operating margin holding near 13.09%, would support buying at the current 244.3–249.71 zone instead of waiting for 238.65.
A close above 258.08, which clears the 251.93–258.08 resistance and the 257.19 20-day average, would end the downtrend case and reopen a swing entry.
A close below 226.88, or quarterly sales growth below 12.09% in the 2027-02-04 report, would move the long-term call from wait to avoid.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait for 238.65; the 3.12% fall to 244.43 broke below the 200-day average of 245.78 without reaching the buy level.
note.label: Research, not advice.

note.headline: Microsoft slips 1.25% to 489.93 on reported outage; support holds, hold stays

summary.thesis: Microsoft's sales and profit margins are still improving, but free cash flow is shrinking and the price needs much faster cash growth than the business shows, so the case for holding rests on that spending paying back.
summary.decision: Long-term: hold, and add only near the bottom of the own-history fair range. Swing: the existing trade stays on, and new entries go in at the top of the first support zone.
summary.act_at: Add at 474.82; swing entry at 485.06, stop 475.34, target 503.99

note.happening: Microsoft fell 1.25% to 489.93. That puts it back inside the 485.58–490.27 zone where it has been trading and just above the 475.34–485.06 support zone. The Verge reported that Microsoft declared a 'Code Red' after a large Outlook outage. The next earnings report is on 2027-01-27, and analysts' earnings estimates have risen 2.19% over the last 30 days.
note.business: The core business is still improving. Sales grew 18.8% from a year earlier in the latest quarter, faster than the 18.3% two quarters ago. Trailing revenue is 346.4B, up from 293.8B. The operating margin, the share of each sales dollar left after running costs, rose to 47.1% from 46.27%. The weak spot is cash. Trailing free cash flow, the cash left after spending on the business, fell to 60.0B from 78.0B, and the free-cash-flow margin is only 17.31%. Free cash flow grew to 11.4B from 9.0B, and operating margin rose to 31.3% from 29.14%.
The share count fell 3.35% in a year, so each remaining share owns more of the business.
bear: Quarterly sales growth slowed to 11.85% from 16.19% two quarters ago.
This quarter's EPS estimate was cut 7.3%, and next year's was cut 1.1% in 30 days.
Operating margin is at the top of its 17–31% five-year range. If it falls to 15%, the value is 39.57.

levels.what: Top of the 56.31–56.81 support zone, the next small add. It is below the 59.9 margin-fade value and the 58.94 own-history low.
Value at 10% starting cash-flow growth and the low end of the fair-value range. This is the last planned add before the report.
DCF base value. Above it the margin of safety is gone, so no buying there.

longterm.why: At 59.41 the price is below the 64.9 DCF base and close to the 59.9 value even if margins fade to 23%. Estimates are still being trimmed and the trend is down, so adds stay small and staggered.

swing.why: The trend is down and the price is under every falling average. The first resistance at 61.14–61.64 is closer than the 56.31 support, so the upside is smaller than the downside. No trade until a close above 65.08.

decision.timing: The 2027-01-19 report comes after the 2027-01-15 option expiry (which prices an 11.4% move) and before the 2027-02-19 expiry (16.9%). So adds stop at the 53.74 slice before the report, and further buying waits for a report that keeps operating margin near 31.3%.

change_mind: If the 2027-01-19 report shows operating margin heading toward 23%, where value is 59.9, stop adding. Toward 15%, where value is 39.57, the decision moves to avoid.
If next-year EPS estimates drop below the 3.56 low end, the 10%-growth value of 53.74 becomes the ceiling, not the floor.
If the price closes above the 64.56–65.08 resistance, the downtrend has broken, and a swing entry becomes possible with a stop under 61.14.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still add; the price of 59.41 remains below the DCF base (now 64.9) and the 59.9 margin-fade value. A new 56.31–56.81 support zone now gives a level for the next slice.
note.label: Research, not advice.
